items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Frank Drake's called me and wanted me to come up to New York and do a session... I was helping him to talk to John Hardy.

ctx.x: He plays now, but he has lost most of his teeth and he's playing on the organ, but he's also

playing. Besides, the other day, Frank Drake's called me and wanted me to come up to New York and do a session and he wanted me to get hold of Buster's number. But I don't know what happened to that thing, Dick. But he wanted to get Buster's number. And I gave him Buster's number. But I don't know what happened to that thing, Dick. I never was called to go to this session. And I was helping him. And I talked to John Hardy. You remember John Hardy? Yeah. And he said, I don't know what happened to that thing. I…
What did Buster Smith sound like then? What did he sound like?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Frank Drake's got all of this information from me.

ctx.x: Well, it's a shame to let all this material not get published, and yet it's hard to find anybody who's interested in it. Right, they're interested in it. And they publish, you know, really second-rate books and all of that. And certainly if anybody knows about Kansas City music and Texas and Oklahoma and all that is Frank Drake. And I think everybody in the business knows that.
Well, Frank Drake's got all of this information from me. Yeah.
But I mean, he's the one who's done the most writing. Right. And then, uh...
